title: Why a White Coat Can Help—and Hurt

scenes.tts: How can the same white coat protect a hare and put it in danger? Watch this Montana hillside change around one hare.
scenes.caption: How can the same white coat protect a hare and put it in danger? Watch this Montana hillside change around one hare.
scenes.visual: Hook first. A large white snowshoe hare fills the center of a split hillside: snow at left, bare brown ground at right. A predator-eye icon searches both halves. Keep a visible 'schematic' label on all drawn animals and settings. COLOUR MAP for both films: matched condition GREEN; mismatch RED; inherited variation BLUE; population and time YELLOW; snow WHITE; bare ground BROWN. The hare shifts slightly between halves while the question appears.
scenes.narration: How can the same white coat protect a hare and put it in danger? Watch this Montana hillside change around one hare.

scenes.visual: The hillside stays full frame. Title 'Why a White Coat Can Help—and Hurt' settles above the moving hare; falling leaves cross the frame.

scenes.tts: Begin in fall. The ground is brown, and the hare is brown too. Its outline blends into leaves and tree shadows.
scenes.caption: Begin in fall. The ground is brown, and the hare is brown too. Its outline blends into leaves and tree shadows.
scenes.visual: Transform the split hillside into one BROWN fall hillside. The hare turns brown and moves through leaf shadows. Its outline briefly glows GREEN, then fades into the background. Label 'match'.
scenes.narration: Begin in fall. The ground is brown, and the hare is brown too. Its outline blends into leaves and tree shadows.

scenes.tts: Now snow covers the hillside. The hare's large back feet spread its weight on soft snow. Fur underneath helps keep those feet warm.
scenes.caption: Now snow covers the hillside. The hare's large back feet spread its weight on soft snow. Fur underneath helps keep those feet warm.
scenes.visual: WHITE snow sweeps across the carried hillside. Zoom to the hare's large back feet pressing shallow prints into soft snow. A close view shows simple fur strokes under one foot. Labels 'large feet' and 'fur underneath' follow the moving foot.
scenes.narration: Now snow covers the hillside. The hare's large back feet spread its weight on soft snow. Fur underneath helps keep those feet warm.

scenes.tts: The hare also grows white winter fur. This coloring is camouflage because it helps the hare blend into its background. Camouflage never makes it invisible.
scenes.caption: The hare also grows white winter fur. This coloring is camouflage because it helps the hare blend into its background. Camouflage never makes it invisible.
scenes.visual: Pull back as the hare's coat gradually changes from BROWN to WHITE. A GREEN outline fades as the coat matches the snow. The predator-eye icon still tracks movement, showing that the hare remains visible. Label 'camouflage'.
scenes.narration: The hare also grows white winter fur. This coloring is camouflage because it helps the hare blend into its background. Camouflage never makes it invisible.

scenes.tts: Spring comes early, but the hare is still white. When the snow disappears, will the hare become harder or easier to spot?
scenes.caption: Spring comes early, but the hare is still white. When the snow disappears, will the hare become harder or easier to spot?
scenes.visual: A warm wind pushes WHITE snow toward the edge, stopping halfway. The white hare remains centered. Two answer arrows appear: GREEN 'harder' and RED 'easier'.
scenes.narration: Spring comes early, but the hare is still white. When the snow disappears, will the hare become harder or easier to spot?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Hold the half-melted hillside and both choices. A ring timer advances while clouds drift slowly.

scenes.tts: The bare ground returns, and the white hare stands out. The predator can notice it more easily. The helpful winter coat now carries a cost.
scenes.caption: The bare ground returns, and the white hare stands out. The predator can notice it more easily. The helpful winter coat now carries a cost.
scenes.visual: Sweep away the remaining snow. A RED outline snaps around the white hare, and the predator-eye icon locks onto it. A balance marker transforms from GREEN 'helps on snow' to RED 'costs on bare ground'.
scenes.narration: The bare ground returns, and the white hare stands out. The predator can notice it more easily. The helpful winter coat now carries a cost.

scenes.tts: An adaptation is an inherited trait that helps survival and reproduction in a particular ecosystem. The coat and feet are physical adaptations.
scenes.caption: An adaptation is an inherited trait that helps survival and reproduction in a particular ecosystem. The coat and feet are physical adaptations.
scenes.visual: Keep the hare large. A family line of parent and young hares moves behind it, linked by BLUE arrows labelled 'inherited'. Brackets point to coat and feet under the label 'physical: body feature'.
scenes.narration: An adaptation is an inherited trait that helps survival and reproduction in a particular ecosystem. The coat and feet are physical adaptations.

scenes.tts: A behavioral adaptation is an action or pattern of actions. Migration is a regular journey between places used in different seasons. The animal does something, rather than having another body part.
scenes.caption: A behavioral adaptation is an action or pattern of actions. Migration is a regular journey between places used in different seasons. The animal does something, rather than having another body part.
scenes.visual: The hillside widens into a simple seasonal map beside the hare. A small group of monarch cartoons follows a curved YELLOW path south. The path animates continuously. Labels contrast 'physical: body feature' with 'behavioral: action'.
scenes.narration: A behavioral adaptation is an action or pattern of actions. Migration is a regular journey between places used in different seasons. The animal does something, rather than having another body part.

scenes.tts: Physical adaptations do different jobs. A heron's long legs reach into deeper water for fish. A turtle's shell shields its soft body from predators.
scenes.caption: Physical adaptations do different jobs. A heron's long legs reach into deeper water for fish. A turtle's shell shields its soft body from predators.
scenes.visual: The seasonal map folds into two large moving silhouettes beside the hare: a heron wades as water rises up its legs, and a turtle withdraws under a domed shell. Both sit under 'physical: body feature'.
scenes.narration: Physical adaptations do different jobs. A heron's long legs reach into deeper water for fish. A turtle's shell shields its soft body from predators.

scenes.tts: Hibernation crosses the simple groups. A groundhog becomes deeply inactive, its heart slows, and its body cools. That is behavior plus a change inside the body.
scenes.caption: Hibernation crosses the simple groups. A groundhog becomes deeply inactive, its heart slows, and its body cools. That is behavior plus a change inside the body.
scenes.visual: Transform the turtle shell into a groundhog burrow under the carried winter hillside. A curled groundhog breathes slowly while a heart icon and temperature bar both fall. Labels 'behavior' and 'body function' join over the same animal.
scenes.narration: Hibernation crosses the simple groups. A groundhog becomes deeply inactive, its heart slows, and its body cools. That is behavior plus a change inside the body.

scenes.tts: A trade-off means a trait helps in one way but costs in another. The white coat works well only when the background fits.
scenes.caption: A trade-off means a trait helps in one way but costs in another. The white coat works well only when the background fits.
scenes.visual: Return fully to the carried hillside. Slide the same white hare between WHITE snow and BROWN ground. The marker changes GREEN on snow and RED on bare ground. Label 'trade-off' above a rocking balance.
scenes.narration: A trade-off means a trait helps in one way but costs in another. The white coat works well only when the background fits.

scenes.tts: The turtle's protective shell is heavy to carry. No living thing is perfectly adapted. Conditions change, and a useful feature can bring a cost.
scenes.caption: The turtle's protective shell is heavy to carry. No living thing is perfectly adapted. Conditions change, and a useful feature can bring a cost.
scenes.visual: The rocking trade-off balance carries a protective shell on one side and a weight icon on the other. The balance keeps moving as the hillside shifts from snow to bare ground. Label 'no perfect fit'.
scenes.narration: The turtle's protective shell is heavy to carry. No living thing is perfectly adapted. Conditions change, and a useful feature can bring a cost.

scenes.tts: Adaptations help in particular settings; populations change over generations, not individuals. One hare cannot choose a new inherited coat because the snow vanished.
scenes.caption: Adaptations help in particular settings; populations change over generations, not individuals. One hare cannot choose a new inherited coat because the snow vanished.
scenes.visual: The rule appears beside the large hare, not as a list. The single hare tries no transformation. Behind it, a YELLOW timeline extends toward a group of hares, preparing the next idea.
scenes.narration: Adaptations help in particular settings; populations change over generations, not individuals. One hare cannot choose a new inherited coat because the snow vanished.

scenes.tts: Hares in one forest are not identical. Some begin changing color earlier than others. These differences among individuals are variation, and they may matter when seasons shift.
scenes.caption: Hares in one forest are not identical. Some begin changing color earlier than others. These differences among individuals are variation, and they may matter when seasons shift.
scenes.visual: Four hare cartoons move onto the YELLOW timeline. Their coats change at different positions, marked by BLUE ticks. Label 'variation'. Keep every timeline mark moving gently past one fixed spring marker.
scenes.narration: Hares in one forest are not identical. Some begin changing color earlier than others. These differences among individuals are variation, and they may matter when seasons shift.

scenes.tts: Variation also appears across places. In some places with little snow, snowshoe hares stay brown all winter. The useful coat still depends on the setting.
scenes.caption: Variation also appears across places. In some places with little snow, snowshoe hares stay brown all winter. The useful coat still depends on the setting.
scenes.visual: Split the carried world into a snowy hillside and a nearby low-snow hillside. A WHITE winter hare moves on snow; a BROWN winter hare moves on bare ground. Both receive GREEN match outlines. Label 'different places'.
scenes.narration: Variation also appears across places. In some places with little snow, snowshoe hares stay brown all winter. The useful coat still depends on the setting.

scenes.tts: So the same coat can hide or expose a hare. Next, the field evidence asks whether that mismatch changes survival across the population. We will also see what the evidence cannot tell us about any one death.
scenes.caption: So the same coat can hide or expose a hare. Next, the field evidence asks whether that mismatch changes survival across the population. We will also see what the evidence cannot tell us about any one death.
scenes.visual: The four hares settle on the BROWN hillside with different coat shades. GREEN and RED match markers pulse over them. A radio-collar signal arcs outward toward a simple data frame, without showing results.
scenes.narration: So the same coat can hide or expose a hare. Next, the field evidence asks whether that mismatch changes survival across the population. We will also see what the evidence cannot tell us about any one death.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Adaptations help in particular settings; populations change over generations, not individuals.'
